title: Waldschmidt 2000 (DALAG), Prop. 12.2, inductive proof, for any E in which 1, x k-free implies x alg. indep.: every matrix over E is k-equivalent to (A B; C 0), A regular or empty
author: @carlok
source: M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Prop. 12.2 (p. 419), by its proof on pp. 420–422, which needs no hypothesis on k, run for any subspace E with property (ii) of Prop. 12.13 in place of a span of algebraically independent elements. DALAG remarks (p. 422) that this proof yields a more general result, where the xᵢ are not assumed algebraically independent (it cites Roy 1989); this is such a generalisation. The hyperplane E₁ of the induction on the dimension of the span of the entries is chosen to contain 1 when possible (DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_split); the step is DiazModulus.dalag_prop_12_2_step. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Th. 6.4 (1): if k ≥ 3 and v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v (k factors) has its coordinates in ℒ̃, then v ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v = a v′ ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ v′ with a ∈ ℒ̃ and v′ ∈ Q̄ᵐ
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 6.4, part 1 (p. 185), complex case, for any m (printed: m ≥ 2), in the coordinates of the basis e_I(1) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ e_I(k), which is defined over Q̄ (p. 170). Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. The printed proof (pp. 185–186) stops at n ≤ 1 and leaves implicit why a lies in ℒ̃; here a = c₀ᵏ is a Q̄-multiple of the coordinate vⱼᵏ. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_power_span_finrank and DiazModulus.fischler_rational_hull. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Under (ii) of DALAG Prop. 12.13, a non-zero finite-dimensional k-subspace F ⊆ E is F₁ ⊕ kx with x ≠ 0 and either F₁ = 0 or x transcendental over k(F₁)
author: @carlok
source: Step of the proof of M. Waldschmidt, Diophantine Approximation on Linear Algebraic Groups, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 326, Springer, 2000, Prop. 12.2 (p. 419; proof pp. 420–422): the choice of x and of E₁ with E₀ = E₁ ⊕ kx (p. 421), and the analogue of Lemma 12.3, (ii) ⇒ (iii) (p. 420), which makes x transcendental over k(E₁) (p. 422). Here E is any subspace with property (ii) of Prop. 12.13, and x is a member other than 1 of a k-basis of k·1 + F that contains 1, so that F₁ contains 1 when 1 ∈ F and F ≠ k·1; for k + E₀ the printed step "x ∉ E₁, hence x is transcendental over k(E₁)" fails whenever 1 lies in the span of the entries but not in E₁. Novelty: none claimed; routine. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: Fischler 2001, Cor. 6.3 (1): for k ≥ 3, every P = Λᵏ with coefficients in ℒ̃, Λ a linear form, lies on a line ℂQ with Q algebraic made of k-th powers of linear forms
author: @carlok
source: S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Cor. 6.3, part 1 (p. 184; proof p. 185): Conjecture 1 (p. 168) for 𝒱(k, m), k ≥ 3, in the form of its non-trivial inclusion, with a vector line ℂQ as the affine subspace defined over Q̄; the other inclusion is immediate. Fischler's ℒ, the Q̄-vector space spanned by 1 and the logarithms of algebraic numbers, is ℒ̃ here. Part 2, a conditional reduction to 𝒱(2, 2), is not formalised. Proved from DiazModulus.fischler_theorem_1_1. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: If k ≥ 2 and every product of k coordinates of v ∈ ℂᵐ lies in ℒ̃, then v₁, …, vₘ span a Q̄-space of dimension at most 2, and at most 1 if k ≥ 3
author: @carlok
source: Step of the proofs of S. Fischler, Orbits under algebraic groups and logarithms of algebraic numbers, Acta Arith. 100 (2001), 167–187, Th. 6.2 and Th. 6.4 (pp. 184–186): their common core, n ≤ 2, and n ≤ 1 for k ≥ 3, with n the dimension of the Q̄-span of the coefficients. The printed proofs apply Th. 2.3 to a symmetric n × n matrix and, for k ≥ 3, Lemma 6.1; here both steps apply Roy's strong six exponentials theorem in product form (DiazModulus.strong_six_exponentials_unconditional) to a 2 × 3 corner, and Lemma 6.1 is not used. Novelty: none claimed; routine. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 18 November 2026 (C. Perassi).
